title: The memoized per-part revision proof lands: the durable formats bump, an old patch is refused by name, and an eager PPTX lifecycle loses a quarter of its instructions
code_state: crates/litchi-pptx: opened/model.rs (the two-tier proof and the PartDigests memo), opened/transaction.rs, opened/patch.rs, opened/mod.rs, opened/remove_plan.rs and opened/cross_copy_plan.rs (the magic bump and the typed refusal), error.rs and lib.rs (DurablePatchFormat and Error::DurablePatchRevisionFormat), package/model.rs and package/codec.rs (the facade carry and its release). docs/adr/0005 amended. No other crate is touched.
reason_codes: change 0652 decision 4 authorizes change 0645's design in full: 'PPTX memoized revision: invalidate the old patches and make the path faster'

the proof is two tiers with three domain strings: a memoized payload digest, a per-part digest over name, content type, payload digest and relationships, and the revision over the sorted per-part digests under litchi-pptx-opened-v2
only the payload tier is memoized, because a part's content type and relationships are not behind its payload Arc and memoizing the whole part digest on that key would answer stalely
the memo retains the payload Arc it keys, which removes the ABA hazard of an address key and is load-bearing rather than an optimization
Part is a public trait whose blob_arc() need not agree with blob(), so a part failing the alias test is never memoized and is hashed exactly as the unmemoized path hashes it

the durable formats bump to LPRM0002 and LPCP0003 and a superseded magic is refused in from_bytes with a new typed error before any header field is read, because a proof in a superseded algebra cannot be source-checked and a silent mismatch would report the package as moved when the format moved
the facade carries the memo, without which the two bare durable-patch replays of an eager lifecycle hash from cold and the design is worth a third of its value
the facade releases the memo at every mutation that publishes no opened-presentation snapshot, so the retention invariant holds unconditionally instead of only between publications

accepted_evidence.counts: callgrind isolation pairs at --warmup 0 --samples 1 and 3, differenced over the two extra samples, per leg for pptx_eager_batch_edit_save, pptx_eager_multi_slide_batch_edit_save, pptx_slide_move_boundary_save, pptx_slide_remove_boundary_save, pptx_real_file_ordinary_save_edit and pptx_real_file_ordinary_save_lifecycle; whole-child totals plus inclusive Ir for the fingerprint subtree and sha2::sha256::compress256, and a per-call-site isolation pair that separates a cold fingerprint from a memoized one on the same leg
accepted_evidence.memo_accounting: a reverted probe build with per-fingerprint hit/miss and bytes-fed counters, run at --samples 1 and 3 on every selector and differenced into an exact per-lifecycle table: the eager deck's commit and both durable-patch replays answer 228 of 229 parts and feed 93,763 bytes against 17,668,953 (0.53%); the 0638/0649 real deck's commit answers 57 of 58 and feeds 37,618 against 792,152 (4.75%); pptx_slide_remove_boundary_save's nine fingerprints per lifecycle collect zero hits
accepted_evidence.memo_resident_bytes: HashMap::capacity accounting at 29, 85 and 221 parts (3,192 / 6,384 / 12,768 bytes), asserted under a bound of 228 bytes per memoized payload
accepted_evidence.verdict_identity: a pairwise oracle over every .pptx fixture under test-data/ (78 fixtures, expanded to 856 packages by the base, a byte-identical re-allocation and nine single-input mutations each): 9,396 ordered pairs agree between packages_equal, the retained v1 revision and the v2 revision, 0 disagreements; plus change 0645's synthetic 11-package corpus at 121 ordered pairs, 0 disagreements
accepted_evidence.format_refusal: a_superseded_slide_removal_patch_is_refused_by_name and a_superseded_cross_slide_copy_patch_is_refused_by_name: forward and inverse of both families under the superseded magic are refused by from_bytes and from_bytes_with_limits with Error::DurablePatchRevisionFormat naming both magics; an unrecognized magic still returns Error::Invalid; the durable byte limit still refuses an over-long superseded input with Error::Limit first
accepted_evidence.suite: cargo test -p litchi-pptx 885 passed 0 failed; cargo test -p litchi --features docx,xlsx,pptx,xls 265 passed 0 failed; cargo test in tools/perf-baseline 540 passed 0 failed 1 ignored; cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy -p litchi-pptx --all-targets, cargo doc -p litchi-pptx --no-deps and python3 tools/non_iwork_gate.py verify all clean. Every capture re-derives its revision the cold way through a debug_assert! and every reused payload digest is recomputed and compared

accepted_costs.durable_format: LPRM0001 -> LPRM0002 and LPCP0002 -> LPCP0003. Every patch of either format serialized by an earlier build stops applying and must be re-planned; there is no migration and no dual read, because the public revision accessors are untyped [u8; 32] and two algebras behind one type would produce a silent false conflict
accepted_costs.error_identity: an input whose first eight bytes are a superseded magic, and which is within the durable byte limit, now returns Error::DurablePatchRevisionFormat from from_bytes instead of parsing (if it was well formed) or instead of its previous refusal (if it was not). Error is #[non_exhaustive] so the variant is additive
accepted_costs.per_part_tier: two extra SHA-256 initialize/finalize pairs and one hash-map insert per part per fingerprint: +3,109,701 Ir per cold fingerprint of the 229-part eager deck (+0.34%, 13,579 Ir per part) and +309,589 Ir per cold fingerprint of the 25-part boundary deck (12,384 Ir per part)
accepted_costs.memory: about 57 bytes per part of resident table per snapshot (12,768 bytes at 221 parts, asserted under a bound of 228 bytes per entry), plus one Arc refcount per memoized payload; the retention invariant keeps the payload bytes themselves at zero extra cost and is asserted directly
accepted_costs.released_memo: the facade releases its memo at every mutation that publishes no opened-presentation snapshot (a typed edit, a presentation materialization, a change-tracking publication), so a caller that interleaves typed edits with opened publications pays a cold hash after each typed edit. This is the safe direction, chosen over change 0645's looser rule, and it is why the retention invariant holds unconditionally
accepted_costs.collision_margin: the tiering offers 2k+1 hash instances instead of one, about 9 bits of the generic 128-bit collision margin at the default max_parts of 256

known_gaps.callgrind_pricing: callgrind runs SHA-256 in software and counts rep movsb per byte, so the instruction percentages here overstate the native cycle share of hashing; the perf stat cycles in timing/ are the counterweight
known_gaps.corpus_reach: the pairwise oracle compares every ordered pair within each fixture's own mutation corpus, not every pair across fixtures; distinctness across unrelated packages rests on the injectivity argument
known_gaps.cold_fingerprint_subtraction: the eager deck's cold-fingerprint cost on the after leg is obtained by subtracting two memoized fingerprints from the capture_internal call-site total, because both a cold capture and a memoized replay enter through capture_internal; the probe justifies the subtraction
known_gaps.unmeasured: no allocation-count, RSS, cold-cache, range-source, concurrency, producer-shaped or cross-platform measurement; the memo's resident cost comes from HashMap::capacity rather than an allocator counter; the harness's allocation binary has no metrics for the ordinary-save family
known_gaps.cross_copy: the cross-package copy path's physical revisions and change 0598's physical_revision cache are untouched and unmeasured; change 0656 owns that path and may consume Snapshot::part_digests directly

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, range-source, concurrency-scaling or cross-platform result
any claim about allocation counts or resident set size: the memo's resident cost comes from HashMap::capacity rather than an allocator counter
